title: Side hustles
paragraphs: Do you have a job? If you do, you'll know the world of work can be tough – long hours, tedious tasks and stress. But it can bring benefits too, such as a regular salary and, sometimes, job satisfaction. Maybe that's why more of us are now taking on a side hustle – another name for a second job.

For some having two jobs is a necessity – a way to make ends meet and provide extra income. But it now seems that more people want to put their skills and passions into practice to make money. These tend to be entrepreneurial young people who want to work on their own projects alongside their main source of income.

According to Henley Business School, around one in four workers run at least one side hustle business, half of which were started in the past two years. Those aged 25 to 34 are most likely to be involved, with 37% thought to run a sideline of some kind. It calculates that the average side hustler makes about 20% of their income through their second job.

But what's interesting is that many millennials are turning their hand to new jobs not just for money and security. Research has found that almost three-quarters of people are following a passion or exploring a new challenge. BBC News spoke to Becci Mai Ford, who works some of the time for a telecommunications company to pay the bills, but spends the rest of her time developing her crafting company Ellbie Co. She says going full-time is "not financially worth it right now but it fuels my creative soul and makes me happy."

Mobile apps have also aided the more commercially minded side hustler. Peer-to-peer firms such as Uber, Deliveroo, Airbnb and TaskRabbit allow users to do everything from odd jobs to renting out homes and parking spaces from their mobile phone.

Of course having a side hustle means you are self-employed - or freelance - which can give you flexibility to work when you like, but it can be risky. You sometimes work on a zero-hours contract and may not get offered enough work. Or what was originally your passion may become more of a chore. However, this could be the best way to try out a new career or follow a passion while not giving up the day job.

vocabulary.entry: tedious tasks /ˈtiːdiəs tɑːsks/ 单调乏味的任务（复数）
vocabulary.example: The job involves a lot of tedious tasks like data entry.
vocabulary.translation: 这份工作包含很多像数据录入这样单调乏味的任务。

vocabulary.entry: job satisfaction /dʒɒb ˌsætɪsˈfækʃn/ 职业成就感；工作满意度
vocabulary.example: Job satisfaction is more important to her than a high salary.
vocabulary.translation: 对她来说，职业成就感比高薪更重要。

vocabulary.entry: side hustle /saɪd ˈhʌsl/ 副业；兼职
vocabulary.example: She started a side hustle selling handmade jewelry online.
vocabulary.translation: 她开启了一份副业，在网上售卖手工首饰。

vocabulary.entry: make ends meet /meɪk endz miːt/ 维持生计；收支相抵
vocabulary.example: He works two jobs to make ends meet for his family.
vocabulary.translation: 他打两份工来维持一家人的生计。

vocabulary.entry: extra income /ˈekstrə ˈɪnkʌm/ 额外收入
vocabulary.example: Her side hustle brings in a steady stream of extra income.
vocabulary.translation: 她的副业为她带来了稳定的额外收入。

vocabulary.entry: put...into practice /pʊt ˈɪntu ˈpræktɪs/ 把……付诸实践
vocabulary.example: It's time to put our plans into practice.
vocabulary.translation: 是时候把我们的计划付诸实践了。

vocabulary.entry: entrepreneurial /ˌɒntrəprəˈnɜːriəl/ adj. 富有创业精神的；企业家的
vocabulary.example: The college offers courses to develop students' entrepreneurial skills.
vocabulary.translation: 这所大学开设课程培养学生的创业技能。

vocabulary.entry: main source of income /meɪn sɔːs ɒv ˈɪnkʌm/ 主要收入来源
vocabulary.example: His salary from the company is his main source of income.
vocabulary.translation: 他的主要收入来源是公司发放的薪水。

vocabulary.entry: sideline /ˈsaɪdlaɪn/ n. 副业；兼职
vocabulary.example: Teaching piano is her sideline apart from her full-time job.
vocabulary.translation: 除了全职工作外，教钢琴是她的副业。

vocabulary.entry: millennials /mɪˈleniəlz/ n. 千禧一代（通常指1981—1996年出生的人）（复数）
vocabulary.example: Millennials tend to value work-life balance more than previous generations.
vocabulary.translation: 千禧一代比前几代人更看重工作与生活的平衡。

vocabulary.entry: turn one's hand to /tɜːn wʌnz hænd tu/ 尝试做；着手做
vocabulary.example: She can turn her hand to almost any kind of creative work.
vocabulary.translation: 她几乎能胜任任何一种创意工作。

vocabulary.entry: telecommunications company /ˌtelikəˌmjuːnɪˈkeɪʃnz ˈkʌmpəni/ 电信公司
vocabulary.example: He works as an engineer in a large telecommunications company.
vocabulary.translation: 他在一家大型电信公司担任工程师。

vocabulary.entry: fuel one's creative soul /ˈfjuːəl wʌnz kriˈeɪtɪv səʊl/ 满足创作热情
vocabulary.example: Painting fuels her creative soul and makes her feel fulfilled.
vocabulary.translation: 绘画满足了她的创作热情，让她感到充实。

vocabulary.entry: commercially minded /kəˈmɜːʃəli ˈmaɪndɪd/ 有商业头脑的
vocabulary.example: He is a commercially minded designer who knows how to sell his works.
vocabulary.translation: 他是个有商业头脑的设计师，懂得如何推销自己的作品。

vocabulary.entry: peer-to-peer /ˌpɪə tə ˈpɪə/ adj. 点对点的；对等的
vocabulary.example: Peer-to-peer lending platforms connect borrowers directly with lenders.
vocabulary.translation: 点对点借贷平台直接对接借款人和贷款人。

vocabulary.entry: odd jobs /ɒd dʒɒbz/ 零散的活儿；杂活（复数）
vocabulary.example: He does odd jobs for neighbors to earn some pocket money.
vocabulary.translation: 他帮邻居做些杂活赚零花钱。

vocabulary.entry: self-employed /ˌself ɪmˈplɔɪd/ adj. 个体经营的；自雇的
vocabulary.example: She is self-employed and runs her own graphic design business.
vocabulary.translation: 她是个体经营者，经营着自己的平面设计工作室。

vocabulary.entry: freelance /ˈfriːlɑːns/ adj. 自由职业的
vocabulary.example: Many writers and designers work as freelance professionals.
vocabulary.translation: 许多作家和设计师都是自由职业者。

vocabulary.entry: zero-hours contract /ˈzɪərəʊ aʊəz ˈkɒntrækt/ 零时工合同（没有固定工时的雇佣合同）
vocabulary.example: A lot of part-time workers are on zero-hours contracts.
vocabulary.translation: 很多兼职人员签订的都是零时工合同。

vocabulary.entry: chore /tʃɔː(r)/ n. 琐事；乏味的工作
vocabulary.example: Washing dishes every day is my least favorite chore.
vocabulary.translation: 每天洗碗是我最不喜欢的琐事。

vocabulary.entry: try out /traɪ aʊt/ 尝试；试用
vocabulary.example: She decided to try out a new recipe for dinner.
vocabulary.translation: 她决定晚餐时尝试一道新食谱。

vocabulary.entry: day job /deɪ dʒɒb/ 正职；日常工作
vocabulary.example: He is a musician in his spare time and has a day job as a teacher.
vocabulary.translation: 他业余时间是一名音乐家，本职工作是教师。

sentences.english: These tend to be entrepreneurial young people who want to work on their own projects alongside their main source of income.
sentences.chinese: 这类人群往往是富有创业精神的年轻人，他们希望在主业之外，经营属于自己的项目。

sentences.english: According to Henley Business School, around one in four workers run at least one side hustle business, half of which were started in the past two years.
sentences.chinese: 据亨利商学院统计，大约四分之一的职场人士至少经营着一份副业，其中半数副业是在过去两年内开启的。

sentences.english: Those aged 25 to 34 are most likely to be involved, with 37% thought to run a sideline of some kind.
sentences.chinese: 25至34岁的人群参与副业的概率最高，约37%的该年龄段人群都有一份副业。

sentences.english: It calculates that the average side hustler makes about 20% of their income through their second job.
sentences.chinese: 数据显示，副业从业者平均约20%的收入来自于副业。

sentences.english: But what's interesting is that many millennials are turning their hand to new jobs not just for money and security.
sentences.chinese: 但有趣的是，许多千禧一代开始尝试新工作，并非仅仅为了金钱和稳定。

sentences.english: She says going full-time is "not financially worth it right now but it fuels my creative soul and makes me happy."
sentences.chinese: 她表示，现在全职经营副业“在经济上并不划算，但这能满足我的创作热情，让我感到快乐。”

sentences.english: Mobile apps have also aided the more commercially minded side hustler.
sentences.chinese: 各类手机应用也为那些有商业头脑的副业从业者提供了助力。

sentences.english: Peer-to-peer firms such as Uber, Deliveroo, Airbnb and TaskRabbit allow users to do everything from odd jobs to renting out homes and parking spaces from their mobile phone.
sentences.chinese: 优步、户户送、爱彼迎和跑腿兔等点对点服务平台，让用户可以通过手机完成各种业务，从零散的跑腿活儿到出租房屋、停车位，一应俱全。

sentences.chinese: 当然，做副业意味着你属于个体经营者——或者说是自由职业者，这种工作模式能让你灵活安排工作时间，但同时也存在风险。

sentences.chinese: 你可能会签订零时工合同，面临工作量不足的问题。

sentences.english: Or what was originally your passion may become more of a chore.
sentences.chinese: 或者，曾经热爱的事业，也可能慢慢变成枯燥乏味的琐事。
